name: errors
description: An error log and alerts: problems are saved, the owner gets an email, crashed pages say sorry and report themselves, and an admin page shows what happened.

envExample.name: CRON_SECRET
envExample.comment:
Scheduled health checks. A private random value the checker sends to /api/ops/summary. Shipyard's ops setup fills this in.
Leave it empty and that page stays closed (it answers "not found").

envExample.name: ERROR_ALERT_HOURS
envExample.comment: Error emails. Hours between two emails about the same problem. Optional, 6 if empty.

patches.note: Add the error check to the Health page: spread errorsHealthChecks (from @/lib/errors/health) into the list of checks.
Add the error log to the admin part of the account menu: add { href: "/admin/logs", label: "Error log" } to the ADMIN_LINKS list in src/lib/nav.ts.

patches.insert: Error log
patches.note: Link the Health page to the error log: add a link to /admin/logs above the list of checks.
List this table of personal data for account deletion in a shared Supabase project: add { table: "error_log", column: "user_id" } to ACCOUNT_DATA_TABLES in src/lib/account/pre-delete.ts.

next: Sign in as the owner and open Error log from the account menu (or /admin/logs). Problems the app hits are saved there; a page that crashes shows a friendly screen and reports itself.

To get an email when something breaks, set ADMIN_EMAIL and the email setup (RESEND_API_KEY). Without them problems are still logged, just not mailed. At most one email per problem every 6 hours (ERROR_ALERT_HOURS).
The scheduled health check needs CRON_SECRET: Shipyard's ops setup creates it and sends it to Vercel and GitHub.
Log rows older than 90 days are deleted every day if Supabase Cron is switched on (Dashboard, Integrations, Cron). Otherwise the scheduled health check deletes them.
In your own routes, catch a failure and call serverError("area", error, "save your changes") from @/lib/errors/report: the visitor sees a plain sentence and you get the real error.
